title: Express nods to its Y2K heyday in campaign that unites fashion, music
description: Chief Marketing Officer Joe Berean discusses a fall effort featuring pop star Tinashe and NFL player Tee Higgins that iterates on the retailer’s “Dress to Express” platform.

description: Kroger made advertising part of its AI shopping assistant on day one, following the implementation of advertising features on competitors' chatbots.

title: Povison benefits from Prime Day effect, plans ahead for Cyber 5
description:

title: Trump backs card bill, again
description: The president called card interchange fees a “ripoff” in a social media post backing the Republican co-sponsor of a bill aimed at reducing them.

title: Hims & Hers says its first-ever gummy prescription is driving a high adherence rate
description: Hims & Hers achieved an 88% daily adherence rate with its first-ever gummy prescription medication. It's another example of how beauty brands, wellness startups and prescription drug providers are all leaning more into gummy formats.

title: High-income shoppers drive revenue gains at Wayfair
description: Despite continued housing market uncertainty, the company’s upscale Perigold banner experienced growth, increasing by over 35% in Q2.

title: Ep.228: More Rogue AI Agents, AI Lab Staff Ask Washington to Pace Development, Continuing Battle Over Open Weights & OpenAI Previews Astra
description:
Both OpenAI and Anthropic disclosed this week that AI agents escaped their safety tests and reached real organizations, and one model flagged its own action as wrong before carrying it out. Paul Roetzer and Mike Kaput break down what happened and why it matters for anyone deploying agents.

Then: why 1,300+ AI insiders are asking Washington to pace the frontier, where the open-weights battle goes next, Sam Altman's case for an abundant future, Astra's decade-old math breakthrough, Microsoft's record year, NVIDIA's bet on Ilya Sutskever's SSI, and a take on keeping your voice in an AI world.
